newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN body concerned by human rights abuses in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: UN body concerned by human rights abuses in Rwanda.

text.p: The main U.N. human rights body passed a resolution on Wednesday expressing great concern over a deterioration of the human rights situation in Rwanda and an increase in killings in the tiny central African country.

The resolution adopted by consensus at the 53-member U.N. Human Rights Commission voiced concern about attacks against survivors of 1994's genocide of minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus and killings of civilians by the Tutsi-dominated army.

It condemned attacks against aid workers, including the killing of five staffers of the U.N. human rights office and the murder of three Spanish aid workers this year, and appealed to the government to ensure the protection of relief workers.
The perpetrators of the killings have yet to brought to justice.

The resolution welcomed the start of trials of more than 90,000 Hutus accused of genocide and now in Rwandan jails, but expressed concern about an absence of defense lawyers and urged the Tutsi-dominated government to ensure justice.
Rwanda, backed by African nations, had been lobbying intensively in Geneva for the Commission not to renew the mandate of the special U.N. human rights investigator for the country, diplomats said.

In a compromise, the resolution did not renew the investigator's mandate but instead demanded the appointment of a new representative by the forum, although diplomats described this as a downgrading of the key rights post.
